# TRIPWIRES
*Generated by `python3 thesis_doc.py` from `out/metrics.json` (data as of 2026-11-09). Every number below is computed by code in this repository; `make verify` rebuilds them with no API key and fails if this file is out of date. Research, not investment advice.*

## The failure rule
On the due date, the thesis (NEAR's price is ahead of what its one paying product returns to holders) is WRONG if at least two of T1, T2, T3 are HIT. It is STRONGER if T4 or T5 is HIT. Anything else leaves it standing. T6 is a data check: if it is a MISS, nothing is scored until the two providers are reconciled.

Each tripwire or forecast can be PENDING (waiting for the due date), HIT (the condition is met) or MISS (the condition is not met). If at least two of T1, T2 and T3 are HIT on their due date, this thesis is wrong.

## Two counterfactuals

**1. If NEAR moved per transaction had not changed, NEAR-denominated transfer volume would have fallen about as far as transactions did.** NEAR moved per transaction is 7.3 times what it was a year ago (`paradox.near_per_txn_x`), so NEAR volume is 1.10 times last year's (`paradox.near_volume_x`) although transactions are 0.15 times last year's (`paradox.txns_x`). At last year's NEAR per transaction, volume would be about 0.15 times last year's, a fall of 85%. The pieces are in the table in THESIS.md, section "The volume paradox, explained".

**2. If buybacks supported the valuation, NEAR's Intents revenue would be far higher.** Tripwire T2 asks for a market cap of 100 times annual Intents revenue or less (threshold read from the T2 row BY ID). At today's market cap of $4.69 billion that needs $46.9 million of revenue a year. NEAR's Intents revenue runs at $22.4 million a year (`intents_daily.revenue_annualised`): 2.1 times short. (Today: $46.9 million needed, 2.1 times short.)

## How NEAR Intents is sampled

The NEAR Intents Explorer API (https://explorer.near-intents.org/api/v0/transactions, statuses=SUCCESS) collects one full UTC day (00:00:00 to 23:59:59) per Sunday. Pages of 1,000 are read until a short page. USD is the sum of each swap's `amountInUsd` as the Explorer reports it. Sample: 53 Sundays from 2025-11-09 to 2026-11-08 (`intents.n_sampled_days`).

This sample is used for swap counts and dollars per swap (`intents.swaps_change_pct`, `intents.usd_per_swap_last4`: last four samples 2,053.71). It is NOT used for any Intents fee, revenue or buyback number — those come from DefiLlama's daily series, every day since 2025-05-10.

No outlier filter is applied, and we have not measured how a Sunday compares with the rest of the week, so the sample shows a direction, not a level.

## Data integrity

T6 compares 365-day gas fees from two providers (today 0.03% apart, `crosscheck.gas_fees_abs_diff_pct`; the 30-day mean price from NearBlocks and CoinGecko differs by less than 0.0001%).

Every data file is listed with its SHA-256 as fetched in `data/SHA256SUMS`. The source files are not shipped (their providers' terms bar republishing or are unclear; see README, 'What is committed, and why'): `python3 fetch.py` downloads them again, and `cd data && sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS` checks the ones you have. `make verify` fails if a file differs from its listed hash or is not listed.

## How to add your own

Add a row to `tripwires.json` or `forecasts.json` with a test and a due date. Run `python3 score.py --forecasts tripwires.json` to score it. If you add a path, make sure metrics.py computes it.
